summary: In this excerpt from Book 12, part 9, Mrs. Enderby reassures the young Lexy Moran that dramatic events are common in life, then shows her a letter from Caroline announcing a secret marriage and asking her parents' forgiveness. Lexy is moved and admits she was foolish, then asks to go for a walk. Mrs. Enderby asks her to return in half an hour and to keep the matter secret, and Lexy leaves puzzled, unable to believe Caroline could have acted without her knowing.
one_line: Mrs. Enderby shows Lexy Moran a letter from Caroline announcing a secret marriage, and Lexy, chastened, goes out for a walk.
key_facts: Mrs. Enderby tells Lexy that at twenty one breaks the heart for a man and at forty one breaks the heart for one's child.
Mrs. Enderby says that in life there is only that and money, and that love and money are nothing else.
Caroline's letter asks her father and mother to forgive her for what she has done.
Caroline writes that she knew her parents would not have let her go if she had told them.
Caroline's letter states that when her parents receive it she will be married.
Caroline promises to write again the next day to tell her parents where she is and to beg them to let her bring her husband to them.
Lexy admits to herself that she was a little fool and that Mrs. Enderby was wise.
Lexy's instinct in any sort of trouble is to get out into the fresh air and walk.
Mrs. Enderby asks Lexy to return in half an hour because there is much to be done.
Mrs. Enderby asks Lexy to say nothing of the matter to any person whatever.
Lexy cannot understand why Mrs. Enderby makes a mystery of the matter, since everyone will know sooner or later.
Lexy finds it hard to believe Caroline ran off because she never dreamed Caroline was interested in any man.
